title: Ember and Oath
premise: Tamsin Dravenmoor has spent his life mapping the unmapped from inside the Hollow Valley, the one place where magic cannot follow — which is exactly why he never suspected his gift of drawing places that don't yet exist is magic at all. When the crown declares a hunt for the gifted and a burned cartographer's apprentice collapses at his door, Tamsin flees the valley for the first time, joining a fugitive network guided by the last dragon, Vaelith, whose dying fire is the only thing keeping the true king, Aldric, from being wholly consumed by the thing wearing his crown. As Tamsin's maps begin reshaping reality, he learns the usurper is a bound echo of the king's own oath, and that ending it may mean erasing the valley — and the self he built there. In the end, Tamsin chooses to redraw the oath itself rather than destroy the man, unbinding Aldric at the cost of his own gift and his maps, and finds belonging not in a place on parchment but among the people who walked the road with him.
about_author: Odile Sterling is the pen name of a former surveyor who spent a decade mapping coastlines before turning to coastlines that do not exist. She writes from a house full of obsolete atlases, and claims her characters arrive the way weather does.

chapters.title: The Edge of the Ink
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. In the Hollow Valley, Tamsin maps a lake that appears the next morning exactly as drawn, unsettling him and his mentor. The beat is quiet unease — the first crack in a life built on the belief that magic stops at the valley's edge.

chapters.title: Proclamations and Ash
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The crown's heralds post the Edict of the Hunt: all gifted persons to be surrendered or burned. A half-dead apprentice, Wren, staggers into Tamsin's workshop carrying a map that bleeds. The beat is fear hardening into decision.

chapters.title: Leaving the Valley
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin smuggles Wren past the valley's boundary stones, feeling magic brush his skin for the first time — and recognizing it as his own. The mentor stays behind, refusing to look back. The beat is grief braided with exhilaration.

chapters.title: Wren's Testimony
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren recounts the purge of the Cartographers' Guild and the king's strange, hollow-eyed decree. Tamsin realizes the hunt is being mapped, region by region, by someone who knows cartography. The beat is dread sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Road That Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Pursued by hunters, Tamsin draws a road on his map in desperation — and the road appears beneath their feet. The gift is confirmed, and it is loud, dangerous, and visible. The beat is terror at his own power.

chapters.title: Vaelith
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. In the Ashreach mountains they meet Vaelith, the last dragon, ancient and dying, her fire guttering like a candle. She names Tamsin 'the mapmaker' and says the kingdom itself is being redrawn. The beat is awe and the weight of destiny.

chapters.title: The Fugitive Network
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The pair reach the Emberhold, a hidden refuge of the gifted, led by the pragmatic rebel Sefa. Tamsin is welcomed for his gift but distrusted for his valley upbringing. The beat is the first taste of belonging — conditional and fragile.

chapters.title: What the Crown Wears
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Intelligence reveals King Aldric issued the edict in a voice that wasn't his; court defectors speak of 'the thing wearing his crown.' Vaelith confirms: the king is bound to an oath-echo, a creature made of his own broken vow. The beat is the enemy taking shape.

chapters.title: First Blood on the Map
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Hunters find the Emberhold using a stolen chart of Tamsin's own making. The refuge burns; Sefa's brother dies. Tamsin understands his gift can be turned against everyone he's met. The beat is guilt and the collapse of easy heroism.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Oath
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin confesses to Vaelith that he drew the stolen chart. She teaches him that every map is a promise, and promises can be unmade — but only by the one who made them. The beat is acceptance of responsibility.

chapters.title: Into the Capital
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Disguised as surveyors for the crown, Tamsin and Wren infiltrate the capital, where the edict's machinery grinds on and gifted children are marched to the pyres. The beat is cold fury at justice perverted into law.

chapters.title: The King in the Mirror Room
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. In the palace's sealed mirror chamber, Tamsin glimpses Aldric — a man of ash and regret, half-consumed, whispering 'finish the oath.' The echo-king sees Tamsin and smiles. The beat is horror and a strange pity.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Survey Office
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren is recognized by a former guildmate turned informer and barely escapes; the network's capital cell is rolled up. Sefa is captured. The beat is the cost of trust and Wren's guilt at being the thread pulled.

chapters.title: The Echo's Bargain
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The echo-king offers Tamsin a bargain: draw the gifted out of hiding and the valley will be spared. Tamsin refuses — but the echo takes his blood from the stolen chart and begins mapping him instead. The beat is the trap closing.

chapters.title: Fire Enough for One Oath
chapters.summary: Vaelith's POV. Vaelith reveals the truth: she swore the original oath with Aldric, and her dying fire is all that keeps the echo from consuming him wholly. To unbind him, her fire must burn the oath away — and her with it. The beat is sacrifice foretold.

chapters.title: Rescue at the Pyre Grounds
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin and Wren assault the pyre grounds to free Sefa before her execution. Tamsin redraws the square itself, walls becoming roads, roads becoming rivers — his most violent act of creation yet. The beat is fury transfigured into purpose.

chapters.title: The Valley in Flames
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Word arrives: the echo-king, using Tamsin's blood-chart, has found the Hollow Valley and is burning it. Tamsin must choose between the last remnant of his old self and the kingdom. The beat is heartbreak as the past burns.

chapters.title: What Tamsin Dravenmoor Is
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. In the ashes of the valley, Tamsin stops running from his identity: he is not a man magic found, but a man who was magic all along, shaped by a place built to hide him. He chooses the fugitives, the dragon, the cause. The beat is identity claimed at last.

chapters.title: The Last Flight
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Vaelith, fire nearly gone, carries Tamsin and Wren to the capital for the final confrontation as the echo begins rewriting the kingdom's borders into a single gray dominion. The beat is the long dark before dawn.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Climax. In the mirror chamber, Tamsin does not destroy the oath — he redraws it, line by line, turning a vow of dominion into a vow of stewardship while Vaelith's last fire burns the old words away. The echo dissolves; Aldric, mortal and weeping, wakes. The beat is triumph paid for in blood.

chapters.title: Ashes and Atonement
chapters.summary: Aldric and Sefa's interwoven POV. Aldric abdicates his hunt, pardons the gifted, and founds a council where Sefa and the survivors hold seats; the law bends toward justice it never contained. Vaelith's ashes are buried beneath a new-mapped grove. The beat is justice built outside the old law.

chapters.title: The Blank Page
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin's gift is spent — his maps no longer come true — and he finds he doesn't mourn it. He opens a school of cartography with Wren, teaching that maps are promises, not prisons. The beat is quiet belonging: home was never a valley, but the people at his table.
